To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the external sector of India is a major source of macroeconomic instability.
the external sector of India has been performing very well.
India is a net importer of goods and a net exporter of services, and that the trade deficit is financed by net inflows of foreign capital.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: 1) the development of the model, which is based on the structural macroeconomic framework, 2) the calibration of the model, and 3) the estimation of the model.
the development and implementation of a new approach for the analysis of financial market data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Indian economy is not a closed economy, but an economy with a significant external sector, which is open to the rest of the world.
the Indian economy has performed well in terms of its external sector, and the current account deficit has been financed by foreign capital inflows.
the current account deficit is not sustainable and the government needs to take steps to reduce it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
India’s external sector is a complex and dynamic system, which is influenced by various factors, both domestic and external, and which in turn affects domestic macroeconomic variables.
the model performs quite well in terms of forecasting and in terms of explaining the data for the period 1970-2007.
the external sector has become more volatile and more open to shocks in the last two decades.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the external sector is an important component of the overall macro economy and its behaviour has to be modelled carefully to ensure that the macro model captures the dynamics and the interactions between the external and the domestic sector.
India’s external sector is highly sensitive to the global economic cycle, especially to the global financial cycle.
there are two important channels through which external shocks are transmitted to domestic macroeconomic performance in the Indian economy.
